CYCLAMEN  EUROP>EUM.

Sow-bread.  Primulacex.


A  plant  indigenous  in  the  south  of  Europe.  The  tincture  is  made  from  the
fresh  root  gathered  in  Autumn.

"The  Cyclamen  Europseum,  or  Sow-bread,  was  extensively  used  in  medicine  by
the  ancients.  Their  descriptions  of  its  properties  are  vague  enough,  but  it  is  re-
markable that  they  ascribe  to  it  a  power  to  afiect  the  uterus  and  its  appendages —
which  ascription  Avas  not  physiologically  verified  until  the  most  recent  provings.

It  used  to  be  considered  that  the  root  of  Cyclamen,  ajiplied  externally,
hastened  difficult  labors,  and  assuaged  the  pains.  Also,  that  to  touch  Cyclamen,
or  take  it  internally,  would  produce  abortion,  or  bring  on  premature  labor."

The  remedy  was  introduced  into  our  Materia  Medica  by  Hahnemann,  and
proved  by  members  of  the  Austrian  Society  of  Homoeopathic  Physicians  at
Vienna.
